scope: ADDITIVE to spec/screens.json — the Mock Lab.

screen.label: Mock Lab
screen.framing: not an analytics screen — the mechanism by which the calibration claim becomes true

arithmetic.consequence: every extra interaction per pick multiplies by 4800, so entry cost decides whether the claim is ever validated

coreDecision.name: the model's prediction is the input device
coreDecision.detail: the five players most likely to go next are rendered as a numbered list; digits 1-5 commit directly, so the common case is one keystroke
coreDecision.compounding: better calibration means its top five covers more picks, which makes logging faster

keys.Backspace: undo last when the field is empty

entryModes.when: the mock site ended on a results grid
entryModes.note: the only mode whose cost does not scale with 160 — market this one

entryModes.when: working from a screenshot or filling gaps

states.note: THE REAL STARTING CASE — leads with 'one draft is an anecdote'
ADDED — not in the brief; paste is the mode most likely to decide whether 30 mocks happen, and a silent wrong fuzzy match would corrupt calibration quietly

states.condition: one mock's calibration — every bucket thin

hardConstraints: predictions are shown as they were made — never retroactively corrected or recomputed with hindsight
off-board players log as player_id = unknown with raw_text kept, and are excluded from calibration rather than dropped
thin buckets (< 50 calls) refuse to interpret rather than drawing a confident reading
Brier score is kept but demoted — the dots are the claim, the score is the measure
no badges, streaks or levels on the progress affordance
screen.headerBudget: Single non-wrapping row that must fit 924px with all 7 state chips reachable. Short state eyebrow with the long form in a title; league line shrinkable with min-width:0 plus a title; chip group flex:0 1 auto with min-width:0 and overflow-x:auto. Assert documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth.

stamp.writtenAt: POST /api/mocks — log time only, never on read
stamp.why: a hash computed at read time is the same defect as a prediction recomputed at read time — always consistent, always meaningless

states.condition: hash matches the league hash now

states.calibration: excluded by default, includable via an explicit toggle

states.condition: hash is null — logged before the field existed
states.why: a mock whose configuration is unknown can be neither honestly included nor honestly excluded; offering the choice would be false precision dressed as control
states.urgency: every mock logged before the field ships is permanently unstampable — at one mock the fix costs nothing, at fifteen the data is permanently ambiguous

groupingKey.note: If the 30-mock target is per configuration (current default) this stamp IS the grouping key for the whole calibration analysis, not a staleness flag.
implications: aggregate is 'pooled within a configuration', never 'pooled across mocks'
a configuration selector heads the aggregate view; default is the current league config
the 30-square array and the evidence ladder both count within the selected configuration
old configurations remain viewable as history, labelled as not describing this league

partialStaleness.principle: Not everything in a stale mock is stale. The draft happened; the picks are facts. Only model outputs are invalidated.
partialStaleness.surpriseNote: SURPRISE is derived from board.overall_rank, which moves with scoring — it is stale, not a fact
partialStaleness.wrongAlternative: marking the whole row stale would imply we are no longer sure what the manager picked

reviewChip.stale: tag chip in --down: 'logged under 10T · 0.5 PPR — your league is now 1.0 PPR'
reviewChip.unknown: tag chip in --dim2: 'configuration not recorded — logged before we stamped mocks'

treatments.calibrationDots: filled dots retained (the observation is real) at --dim2, --hatch behind the dot row, dagger after the observed value, dimmed reading; the marker stays at full contrast
treatments.frozenBanner: unchanged — predictions are still shown as they were made

mixedAggregate.toggle: Include other configurations — stale set only
whenOn: every bucket row takes the stale treatment
header states which configurations are mixed and in what proportion
Brier score SUPPRESSED — replaced by 'not computed across mixed configurations'
mixedAggregate.brierRationale: a single score spanning two scoring systems is not a worse number, it is not a number

allStale.treatment: aggregate empty form, not an error state
allStale.copy: 0 of 8 mocks describe your current configuration. Calibration for 10T · 1.0 PPR starts from zero. Your eight logged mocks are still here and still valid for the configuration they were logged under — switch configuration above to read them.
allStale.rationale: the harshest consequence of per-configuration targeting; softening it would misrepresent how much evidence exists

treatments.banner: StatusBanner stale variant whenever the selected configuration is not the league's current one

requirements: predicted_* are write-once — reject an update rather than overwrite
raw_text retained on every row so a bad match stays auditable

api.requirement: must return PER-ROW resolution, not just an aggregate count
counts, never percentages — the client computes the Wilson interval

requirements: config_state is derived server-side (current|stale|unknown) so the client never re-implements the comparison
must accept a config hash — a pooled-across-everything response has no honest use

checks.assert: Digits 1-5 commit the corresponding candidate without touching the mouse
checks.probe: focus the input, dispatch keydown '2'
checks.expect: pick logged, field cleared, counter advanced

checks.assert: Backspace on an empty field undoes the last pick
checks.probe: log a pick, clear field, dispatch Backspace
checks.expect: pick count decremented

checks.assert: Tempo readout derives from real entry timestamps
checks.probe: log two picks with a known delay
checks.expect: seconds-per-pick reflects the delay, not a constant

checks.assert: A prediction shown in review is never recomputed
checks.probe: change board state, reload review
checks.expect: predicted_p unchanged

checks.assert: Review carries an explicit 'as they were made' statement
checks.probe: read the review banner
checks.expect: present, not a footnote

checks.assert: Each calibration row shows filled dots for observed and a marker at the stated probability
checks.probe: count filled dots and read marker offset
checks.expect: filled = round(observed/n*10); marker left = stated/100*140-4 px

checks.assert: Calibration direction is carried by marker position and a sentence, not colour alone
checks.probe: desaturate and read a miscalibrated row
checks.expect: direction still legible

checks.assert: Buckets under 50 calls are hatched and refuse to interpret
checks.probe: read a thin bucket's reading text
checks.expect: 'too few calls to read', hatch on the count

checks.assert: Brier score is present but visually subordinate to the dot rows
checks.probe: compare font size and position
checks.expect: Brier in a secondary card, dots in the primary table

checks.assert: An unmatched paste row commits as unknown with raw text, never silently dropped
checks.probe: paste a garbled name, parse, inspect the row
checks.expect: no-match status, raw text retained, excluded-from-calibration note

checks.assert: Fuzzy matches are flagged for review, not auto-committed as exact
checks.probe: paste a misspelling, parse
checks.expect: 'fuzzy' status with a fix affordance

checks.assert: Progress-to-30 shows no badge, streak, level or congratulatory copy
checks.probe: read the aggregate progress block
checks.expect: squares + band width only

checks.assert: The one-mock state states that nine calls cannot validate the claim
checks.probe: read 02-one-logged
checks.expect: explicit statement present

checks.assert: The entry field holds focus on load, and focus is re-asserted if the input node re-attaches
checks.probe: document.activeElement on load, then after a re-render
checks.expect: the entry input in both cases
checks.note: a one-shot ref guard that fires before the element is focusable silently leaves this false — the screen claims 'never needs the mouse' directly beneath the field

checks.assert: The header does not force horizontal document scroll at 924px, and all 7 state chips are reachable
checks.probe: documentElement.scrollWidth vs clientWidth; right edge of the last chip
checks.expect: equal widths; last chip right edge inside the viewport

checks.assert: Any truncated header text carries the full string in a title attribute
checks.probe: for each header span: scrollWidth > clientWidth implies title present
checks.expect: no truncation without a hover fallback

checks.assert: Every mock carries league_settings_hash written at log time
checks.probe: POST a mock, read the record
checks.expect: hash present and equal to the league hash at that moment

checks.assert: A mock with a null hash is excluded from calibration and offers no way to include it
checks.probe: seed an unknown-config mock, inspect the aggregate and its controls
checks.expect: counted as excluded (unrecorded); no include affordance

checks.assert: On a stale mock, fact columns stay fresh and only derived columns take the stale treatment
checks.probe: open a stale mock's review
checks.expect: ACTUAL PICK/TEAM/POS at full contrast; WE SAID/OUR TOP CALL/VERDICT/SURPRISE hatched

checks.assert: Including other configurations suppresses the Brier score entirely
checks.probe: toggle include-stale on
checks.expect: 'not computed across mixed configurations', no numeric score

checks.assert: When every mock is stale the aggregate renders its empty form, not an error
checks.probe: change league scoring, open the aggregate
checks.expect: '0 of N mocks describe your current configuration' plus a configuration selector

checks.assert: The aggregate header always states included and excluded counts by reason
checks.probe: read the aggregate header
checks.expect: included · excluded (different configuration) · excluded (configuration not recorded)

founderDecisions.question: Does offering the model's top five bias the logged data?
founderDecisions.why: presenting our own prediction as the fastest key risks logging what we guessed rather than what happened; the fix trades away the entry speed the whole screen depends on

founderDecisions.question: Is 30 the right target, and is it per league or global?
founderDecisions.why: a 10-team half-PPR mock may not validate a 12-team full-PPR league; per-league multiplies the grind
founderDecisions.consequence: the settings hash becomes the grouping key for calibration, not merely a staleness flag

founderDecisions.question: Do other users' mocks count toward calibration?
founderDecisions.recommendation: keep the personal view primary, treat pooled as a separate labelled number
founderDecisions.why: pooling reaches 30 far faster and is the obvious growth loop, but changes the claim from 'calibrated for you' to 'calibrated on average'

founderDecisions.question: Is a partial mock (rounds 1-6) worth logging?
founderDecisions.recommendation: accept, and record rounds_logged so calibration can weight or filter
founderDecisions.why: rounds 1-6 carry nearly all the availability decisions and cost a third as much

backendQuestions.q: Can predicted_top and predicted_p be written at entry time and made immutable?
backendQuestions.impact: the entire review and calibration design rests on it; if predictions can only be recomputed on read, both sections are invalid
backendQuestions.answered: yes — immutable predicted_top/predicted_p at entry was already specified

backendQuestions.q: Is there a bulk pick endpoint, and does it return per-row resolution?
backendQuestions.impact: the reconcile table needs per-row exact/fuzzy/none, not an aggregate count

backendQuestions.q: Does the player matcher exist server-side, or does the client fuzzy-match?
backendQuestions.impact: the reference matches client-side against 70 players; against 378 with nicknames and suffixes this should be a server endpoint

backendQuestions.q: Can a pick store player_id = unknown plus raw_text?
backendQuestions.impact: required so off-board players are excluded from calibration rather than dropped
without it the tempo readout and the 'logged in 6m 12s' figure are not real numbers and must be removed

backendQuestions.q: Are validation buckets available per-mock as well as pooled?
